observed.title: Excalidraw Whiteboard
observed.description: Excalidraw is a virtual collaborative whiteboard tool that lets you easily sketch diagrams that have a hand-drawn feel to them.

insights.summary: excalidraw.com scores 79 out of 100 (C). 4 checks fail now, 13 are at risk, and 20 pass. Fix first: the viewport stops people from zooming.

findings.title: The viewport stops people from zooming
findings.evidence: The viewport tag sets user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.
findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag.

findings.title: Buttons must have discernible text
findings.evidence: axe-core 4.14.0 found 1 element on /, for example #radix-\:re\:. Impact: critical.
findings.fix: Give each icon button visible text or an aria-label.

findings.title: AI crawlers see an almost empty start page
findings.evidence: The HTML carries 10 characters of readable text and an empty app root, so the content is drawn by JavaScript. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript.
findings.fix: Render the main content on the server or pre-render it at build time.

findings.title: Elements must have their visible text as part of their accessible name
findings.evidence: axe-core 4.14.0 found 1 element on /, for example .reset-zoom-button. Impact: serious.
findings.fix: Start the aria-label with the words that are visible on the control.

findings.title: No Organization or Person entity describes who is behind the site
findings.evidence: AI answers lean on this to name the brand, its logo, and its profiles.
findings.fix: Add Organization (or Person) JSON-LD with name, url, logo, and sameAs. The fix kit has a draft.

findings.title: Other sites can frame the page
findings.evidence: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors was sent, so the page can be framed for clickjacking.
findings.fix: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for old browsers).

findings.title: A missing page answers 200 instead of 404
findings.evidence: A made-up path answered 200 with the title "Excalidraw Whiteboard". Search engines call this a soft 404 and may index empty pages.
findings.fix: Return status 404 (or 410) for unknown paths, with a helpful page.

findings.title: No content security policy
findings.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
findings.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

findings.title: /llms.txt answers with an HTML page
findings.evidence: The address returns a web page, which usually means a catch-all route.
findings.fix: Serve a plain-text /llms.txt. The fix kit has a draft built from this read.

findings.title: No security.txt
findings.evidence: /.well-known/security.txt answered with a web page instead of a text file. Researchers who find a flaw have no published way to report it.
findings.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Expires. The fix kit has a draft.

findings.title: 1 page has no main landmark
No structured data was found
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD block was found on the pages that were read.
findings.fix: Add Organization or Person, WebSite, and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. The fix kit has a draft.

findings.title: No content is shaped as questions and answers
findings.evidence: No heading on the pages read is a question and no FAQ data was found. AI answers favour short, direct answers under a question.
findings.fix: Add an FAQ block with the questions customers ask, answered in two or three sentences each.

findings.title: Pages do not say who wrote them or when they were updated
findings.evidence: Author and date signals help search engines and AI answers judge whether a page is current and credible.
findings.fix: Show an author and a last-updated date on content pages, and add them to the JSON-LD.

findings.title: No known analytics tag is in the HTML
findings.evidence: None of 26 known analytics tools appeared in the HTML of the pages read. A tag injected later by a script would not show here.
findings.fix: If visits matter, add a measurement tool. A cookieless one such as Plausible or Cloudflare Web Analytics avoids a consent banner.

findings.title: Core Web Vitals need improvement for real visitors
findings.evidence: Real Chrome users over the last 28 days on this page, at the 75th percentile: Largest Contentful Paint 2.6 s (needs improvement), Interaction to Next Paint 272 ms (needs improvement), Cumulative Layout Shift 0 (good). Source: Chrome UX Report through PageSpeed Insights.
findings.fix: Make the largest element arrive sooner: preload the hero image, serve it at the shown size in a modern format, and cut render-blocking scripts. Break up long JavaScript tasks behind clicks and taps, and defer third-party scripts.

findings.title: Lighthouse scores performance 62/100 on mobile
findings.evidence: Lighthouse 13.5.0 on a simulated mid-range phone over slow 4G: Largest Contentful Paint 7.7 s, Total Blocking Time 40 ms, Cumulative Layout Shift 0, Speed Index 5.4 s.
findings.fix: Open PageSpeed Insights for this URL and work through its opportunities, largest savings first.

cases.title: The reviewed URL answers over https
cases.why: The final URL was https://excalidraw.com/ with status 200. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load.

cases.title: The document has a title
cases.why: A title is present: Excalidraw Whiteboard. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load.

cases.title: The document has one clear h1
cases.why: One h1 was found. Heading text would be compared with the visible hero, not only the tag count.

cases.title: The html element declares a language
cases.why: lang="en" is present. The declared language would be checked against the visible copy.

cases.title: Primary controls have an accessible name
cases.why: 26 button elements were counted. A later run would open a real browser, keep the same host, and assert the step without submitting a form or generating load. Empty buttons and icon-only controls would fail.

cases.title: Discovered pages keep a successful document status
cases.why: 1 saved pages stayed in the success range. A regression run would fail on a new 404 or 500 inside the same path list.

cases.title: Each saved page keeps a title
cases.why: Every saved page had a title. Titles would be asserted per path, including pages reached through one link.

cases.title: The meta description is present and short enough to read
cases.why: A description of 127 characters is present. The useful band for a snippet is about 50 to 160 characters.

cases.title: A canonical link points at the preferred URL
cases.why: Canonical is https://excalidraw.com. The preferred URL would be compared with the final https address of this read.

cases.title: Open Graph and Twitter cards describe the same page
cases.why: Open Graph tags are present. No Twitter card tag was found. A later case would assert og:title, og:image, and the card type.

cases.title: Structured data is valid when the page publishes it
cases.why: No JSON-LD block was found. The type would be checked against the visible page, for example an organization, article, or product.

cases.title: The h1 and the title agree
cases.why: The first h1 is "Excalidraw". The title and the h1 do not have to be identical, and they should not describe different pages.

cases.title: Same-host links discovered from the start page resolve
cases.why: 0 same-host links were listed. This review opened at most 20 of them and did not click them. A later run would request each href and accept only an HTML document on this host.

cases.title: The crawl stays inside the page cap and the host
cases.why: 1 HTML pages were saved, 2 links deep at most, with a cap of 20 pages. A regression would fail if a link left the host or if the cap stopped hiding a broken primary path.

cases.title: A crawler honors robots.txt for linked pages
cases.why: No linked URL was skipped for robots.txt during this read. The start URL is still fetched. A later crawler case would log each skipped path.

cases.title: Images expose a text alternative
cases.why: 0 images, 0 without an alt attribute. Informative images need text. Decorative images need an empty alt.

cases.title: The page has a main landmark and a skip link
cases.why: No main element was found. No skip link was found. The review's headless browser runs axe-core on the rendered page.

cases.title: Heading order follows h1 then h2
cases.why: 1 h1 and 0 h2 elements were counted. The order would be checked in the rendered accessibility tree.

cases.title: Text contrast and keyboard focus are checked on the rendered page
cases.why: Contrast is measured by axe-core in the review's headless browser. Focus order still needs a person: the case would tab from the top of the page and record the focus ring.

cases.title: HTTPS is the only way in
cases.why: The review refused any URL that was not https on port 443. A browser case would also request the http address and expect a redirect to https.

cases.title: HSTS is set
cases.why: strict-transport-security is present. The later assertion is max-age, includeSubDomains, and a fresh profile that stays on https.

cases.title: A content security policy is set
cases.why: content-security-policy was absent. The policy would be checked for script-src and frame-ancestors, not only for the header name.

cases.title: nosniff and a frame policy are set
cases.why: x-content-type-options: nosniff. x-frame-options: absent. A framed copy of the page would be expected to fail when a frame policy is present.

cases.title: Referrer-Policy is set
cases.why: referrer-policy is origin. The later case would open an outbound link and confirm the referrer is no wider than the policy.

cases.title: Response headers do not need to reveal the server build
cases.why: Server header: Vercel. The case records the header and does not treat a product name as a vulnerability by itself.

cases.title: A permissions policy limits powerful features
cases.why: A permissions policy is present. Camera, microphone, and geolocation would be expected to stay disabled unless the page needs them.

cases.title: The HTML does not reference plain http resources
cases.why: 0 scripts, images, frames, or stylesheets load over plain http. Mixed content would be confirmed in a browser console, not by downloading those URLs here.

cases.title: A privacy notice is linked from the page
cases.why: No privacy or legal wording was found in the markup. Confirm the link in a browser before treating it as found.

cases.title: Third-party scripts are named before they run
cases.why: 0 other hosts were referenced by script src. A privacy case would load the page with tags blocked and then with consent.

cases.title: A consent notice is present when tags or cookies appear before a choice
cases.why: Cookie or consent wording was found in the HTML. The case would assert the notice before analytics storage is written.

cases.title: Title, description, canonical, and social tags agree
cases.why: Title and description were read from the HTML. Open Graph tags would be asserted in a later browser case against the same final URL.

cases.title: A sitemap is advertised from the page or robots.txt
cases.why: The word sitemap appears in the HTML. The review fetches the sitemap from robots.txt or /sitemap.xml and compares it with the pages it read.

cases.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the site
cases.why: robots.txt would be read for OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, and Claude-User. A full Disallow for any of them keeps the site out of the answers that product writes. Training crawlers are a separate choice and are not asserted here.

cases.title: llms.txt lists the pages that matter, under a one-line summary
cases.why: The case fetches /llms.txt and expects a > summary line, the layout llmstxt.org proposes. It is a convention some AI tools read, not a ranking factor.

cases.title: The main heading and text are in the HTML before scripts run
cases.why: 1 words of text were in the served HTML, around an empty app root. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they quote only what the server sends.

cases.title: An Organization or Person entity names who is behind the site
cases.why: No JSON-LD was found on the start page. AI answers use the entity to name the brand, its logo, and its profiles.

cases.title: Questions customers ask are answered under question headings or FAQ markup
cases.why: 0 heading(s) on the start page are phrased as a question. Answer engines favour a short answer under the question it answers.

cases.title: Content pages show when they were published or changed
cases.why: No published or modified date was found on the start page. No author is named, which the report lists separately. Search engines and AI answers weigh whether a page is current.

cases.title: The HTML document arrives inside a stated budget
cases.why: This read took 375 ms and 6862 bytes. That is one fetch, not a load test. A budget case would fail above 800 ms or 1.5 MB for the document alone. Lighthouse, through PageSpeed Insights, scores the rendered start page in the Performance findings.

cases.title: Script and stylesheet counts stay inside a budget
cases.why: 1 external scripts and 1 stylesheets were referenced. The later case would record the counts and the render-blocking ones.

cases.title: The slowest page in this read stays inside the same budget
cases.why: The slowest saved response was / at 375 ms. The trend across the crawl is the order the pages were opened, not a history of previous days.

cases.title: An authorised baseline could repeat the document fetch
cases.why: JMeter, Gatling, or k6 would need written permission, a verified domain, and a scheduled window. This review did not open a single virtual user. The baseline would be one request per second for a few minutes.

cases.title: A ramp would add users only inside an agreed ceiling
cases.why: The proposal is a short ramp, then a hold, then a stop. Error rate and response time would be the gates. No profile is generated by this review.

cases.title: A spike would last seconds, not an open-ended flood
cases.why: A spike case belongs on a staging host or a window the owner schedules. The public read here is still one document at a time.

cases.title: The layout holds at a phone width
cases.why: A viewport meta tag is present. Appium or Maestro would open a phone profile later and compare the same h1 and primary link.

cases.title: The same primary path works in a tablet width
cases.why: Width, orientation, and a touch scroll would be checked in Appium, Maestro, or a browser device profile. This HTML read did not resize a window.

cases.title: The lang attribute matches the copy a person reads
cases.why: Declared language: en. A bilingual page would need hreflang plus a visible language switch.

cases.title: A missing path returns a deliberate not-found page
cases.why: This read did not save a 404. A later case would request one unknown path and expect a branded not-found document, not a stack trace.

cases.title: A slow document fails the case instead of hanging the suite
cases.why: This review stops a single page at 8 seconds. A suite would use its own timeout and a screenshot of the last frame.

cases.title: A repeat visit can reuse a cache policy the response already states
cases.why: cache-control is present. The later case would record the header. It would not flush a shared cache.

cases.title: The page still explains itself when scripts do not run
cases.why: A noscript element is present. The case would disable JavaScript and check that the title and the main heading remain.

cases.title: The named stack is recorded with the case
cases.why: Markers seen in this read: Google Fonts, Vercel. The case list is filtered by the frameworks you select. Those tools are not launched. A later cross-browser pass could use BrowserStack. It is not started here.

cases.title: An advertised manifest still leaves the page readable in a normal tab
cases.why: A manifest link is present. The case would open the page in a browser tab and confirm the title and the main heading. It would not install the app.

cases.title: Images reserve their box before they paint
cases.why: 0 images had neither width nor height in the markup. Applitools or Percy would own a later visual diff. The review's headless browser measures layout shift on the start page.

cases.title: The first view stays inside the width the viewport asks for
cases.why: A viewport meta tag is present. The later case would open that width and look for a horizontal scroll on the main content.
